routes.title: PAPADOPOULOS · REGIME & LIBERALISATION
routes.gate: Nationalist military junta in office AND Papadopoulos is the actual ruling leader.
notes: A controlled opening is a risky political proposal, not a completed democracy. Refusal by opposition and officer obstruction remain possible.
Security tutelage preserves officer leverage and the documented coercive state; the rights grievance remains.
Tourism produces investment but dependence on seasonal foreign earnings.
Export credit trades slower visible consumption gains for productive capacity.
European institutions and other players must accept terms; never grants automatic membership.
A patron must actually agree; military access and influence have an explicit price.

routes.title: IOANNIDIS · SECURITY RULE
routes.gate: Nationalist military junta in office AND an actual domestic leadership change has placed Ioannidis in power; Gizikis may be formal president.
names: Keep the Guard out of Politics
notes: ESA policing and torture are named explicitly. Surveillance can consolidate the ruler while increasing security costs and unresolved opposition grievances.
A broader compact improves coordination but reduces the ruler’s personal control.
Priority procurement crowds out civilian investment; no free divisions or weapons.
Civilian orders maintain the tax and industrial base.
A covert approach sends a proposal into the Cyprus/Greek-officer crisis system. Only actual accepted preparation can enable a coup; Turkish/Greek-Cypriot responses are independent.
Restraint can break with hardliners; no scripted invasion is needed to make the choice meaningful.

routes.title: KANELLOPOULOS / KARAMANLIS · ERE → ND
routes.gate: Conservative civilian government in office, an actual electoral/constitutional mandate and the appropriate contemporary leader. ERE before4October1974; ND only after its actual formation.
notes: Accountability reduces the security-state legacy after actual judicial implementation; temporary officer resistance remains a political risk.
Amnesty eases bargaining with the army but leaves victim claims unresolved and cannot also claim the accountability reward.
Competition supports productive exporters without an automatic foreign subsidy.
State enterprises retain strategic capacity with recurring administrative costs.
Association/entry requires counterpart consent and implemented legal conditions. Greece is not an EEC member in1970.
Domestic readiness is a viable economic route if European players decline.

routes.title: MAVROS · THE LIBERAL CENTRE
routes.gate: Liberal civilian party in office and a genuine parliamentary mandate. Centre Union; Centre Union–New Forces only in its contemporary phase.
notes: Judicial accountability follows civilian due process, not arbitrary collective punishment.
Reconciliation can reduce polarisation while retaining obligations to victims.
Competition and public tenders break protected financial networks.
Social credit broadens access but requires a funded guarantee scheme.
Counterpart agreement is necessary; no instant European accession.
Mediation requires participation by the other states; it cannot order them to settle Cyprus.

routes.title: ANDREAS PAPANDREOU · PAK → PASOK
routes.gate: Social-democratic government in office, legal party competition and an electoral mandate. PAK opposition before1974; PASOK requires its actual formation, no earlier than3September1974.
notes: A parliamentary route recognises pluralism and preserves competitive elections.
Executive centralisation speeds programme coordination while increasing administration and patronage risks.
Public provision is an ongoing spending commitment, not free stability or free healthcare.
Targeted transfers leave some urban needs unmet but concentrate scarce funds.
US/NATO players can accept or decline renegotiated access. No forced foreign base removal.
Non-alignment is an alternate policy requiring actual trade arrangements; it never creates Soviet aid.

routes.title: KOLIGIANNIS / FLORAKIS · KKE
routes.gate: KKE legally holds executive power through an actual mandate or a separately resolved domestic revolution. Koligiannis beforeDecember1972, Florakis thereafter; no automatic communist takeover.
notes: The coalition retains political competition; this is distinct from a one-party state.
A vanguard state concentrates authority and introduces new repression risks. It cannot also claim pluralist legitimacy.
Cooperative management decentralises decisions and needs skilled administration.
Central planning can mobilise investment but carries administrative and allocation costs.
Trade diversification requires actual agreements, not gifted resources or factories.
The Soviet player must accept any security agreement; alignment has a sovereignty cost and never spawns an ally army.

routes.title: CONSTANTINE II · A CONTESTED RESTORATION
routes.gate: A monarchy has actually been restored through a valid constitutional settlement. The exiled king is not the starting government and the regent is not a party leader.
names: A Settlement beyond the Failed Counter-Coup
The Settlement Put to the Voters
notes: A constitutional monarch accepts parliamentary supremacy and civilian oversight.
Royal prerogative revives opposition and officer-network risks; restoration is not universal support.
Regional funds decentralise credit through audited eligibility.
Palace direction concentrates strategic capital but creates patronage costs.
European partners judge the constitutional arrangement and may refuse talks.
Bilateral guarantees need the named foreign players; there is no automatic royal alliance.

starting_spirits.title: Rule by Decree
starting_spirits.note: Suspended freedoms and decree government. Administrative coercion is not democratic legitimacy; institutional reform removes this package.

starting_spirits.title: Censorship, Detention and Torture
starting_spirits.note: Military courts, censorship, arbitrary detention and documented torture under the dictatorship. Victims and responsibility remain explicit; repression cannot erase the resulting grievance.

starting_spirits.title: A Politicised Officer Corps
starting_spirits.note: Personal networks, loyalty promotions and competing junta circles disrupt professional command. Not a claim that Greek soldiers are inherently ineffective.

starting_spirits.title: European Censure
starting_spirits.note: Greece left the Council of Europe on12December1969 after the Greek Case. This is not expulsion from NATO or from a nonexistent1970 EU membership.

starting_spirits.title: Uneven Regional Development
starting_spirits.note: Rural skills, fragmented holdings and weak local links limit convergence. Applied only to selected owned rural states, not every Greek resident.

starting_spirits.title: Clientelism and Fragmented Administration
starting_spirits.note: Fragmented administration and patronage impose costs. Audits and professional recruitment reduce these; an ethnic group never constitutes the penalty.

starting_spirits.title: Foundations of the Greek Expansion
starting_spirits.note: Industrial expansion, shipping, tourism and emigrant remittances provide real strengths in1970. Values are gameplay proposals, not measured historical growth rates.

starting_spirits.title: A Crown in Exile
starting_spirits.note: ConstantineII remains in exile and Zoitakis is regent inJanuary1970. A negotiated constitutional settlement or legitimate referendum can settle the issue.

starting_spirits.title: Oil Import Shock
starting_spirits.note: Conditional external supply/price shock, never a January1970 starting penalty. A world oil shock or actual import disruption must occur.

starting_spirits.title: Mobilisation and Civilian Dislocation
starting_spirits.note: Only actual mobilisation, fighting or displacement can activate this. Losses and humanitarian needs are recorded once, not paid for twice by overlapping systems.

rules: All political focuses require the actual governing party/leader, not merely an outlook.
Programme bonuses occupy replacement slots; parties cannot stack seven governments’ institutional/economic bonuses.
No forced coups, wars, treaty changes or guaranteed foreign acceptance. Only Cyprus AI follows the separate dedicated historical path.
Seven days per native focus point. All numeric effects are balance proposals, not historical measurements.
No foreign factories, aircraft, resources, loans or alliance memberships appear without actual contract implementation.
Cyprus and Aegean civilian harm is conditional, recorded once and not erased by coercion.
